narrative.northStar: A record sleeve you can play
narrative.overview:
The website expresses Oma Beats as a record sleeve around the actual playable product interface: broad cream paper, a sage control surface, dark olive text, and orange actions. Condensed display lettering creates the expressive scale; quiet body typography leaves room for a dense, usable music interface. The shared brand commitment is the established cream, sage, and orange identity.

This record scopes its normative marketing tokens and component rules to `site/index.html`, `site/style.css`, `site/fonts.css`, and `site/site.js`. The playable preview embeds the real app renderer in an iframe at `/play/`, generated by `scripts/build-site.cjs` with browser-only integration in `site/browser-preview.js` and `site/browser-preview.css`. The app under `app/` remains a separate incumbent visual surface, including when embedded: it retains Inter/Liberation Sans, monospace readouts, cream gradients, sage LCDs, and its own controls and depth. Do not treat the website's Barlow pairing, size ramp, or exact colors as a migration instruction for the app.
keyCharacteristics: Cream editorial space around a sage instrument.
Condensed display type paired with readable Barlow marketing copy.
Orange for emphasis, actions, and active playback.
The live app renderer, an authentic capture fallback, code-drawn music diagrams, and SVG marketing icons.

rules.name: The Actuation Rule
rules.body: Use orange for a deliberate emphasis, action, or sounding state; keep the broad equipment surface sage.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Use Barlow Condensed for editorial headings and Barlow for marketing instructions and actions. Preserve the app’s own typography inside the embedded renderer.

rules.name: The Equipment Depth Rule
rules.body: Preserve the app’s own tactile depth inside the renderer; use the soft preview shadow at its page boundary. Keep editorial rows flat.

dos: Do preserve the cream, sage, and orange brand relationship across surfaces.
Do use the website tokens only within the website scope unless an app change is explicitly requested.
Do use the real renderer for playable product previews, with an authentic loading/no-JavaScript capture and a full-size player link.
Do use inline SVG icons and code-drawn waveform, pad-bank, and keyboard diagrams.
Do preserve visible focus and accessible control names; keep marketing reduced-motion behavior and app behavior scoped to their respective stylesheets.
Do keep the small-screen sequencer horizontally scrollable inside its own track.
donts: Don't introduce decorative kickers or eyebrows as a reusable heading pattern; compact labels belong to actual controls or product metadata.
Don't use orange as an all-over equipment background.
Don't replace the real renderer with a separately styled simplified demo, represent browser-only availability as native capability, or trigger audio automatically.
Don't invent app UI in product imagery or substitute glyphs for the website’s SVG icons. Authentic app captures are supported.
Don't turn the website's exact first-page composition into a rule for every future surface.
